critique: The render now has a clean pale-blue particle sheet, strong black negative space, and subtle evolving wave motion between t1 and t4. It is much closer to the intended controlled plane than the earlier bokeh-heavy versions. However, it still reads primarily as sharply resolved granular dots rather than a cohesive, softly radiant magical surface. The t4 center also sags into a noticeably broad underside/tail, so the sheet loses some of the thumbnail's refined thin-horizon silhouette.

suggestions.why: Increase the existing glow contribution so the dense particle band merges into a more ethereal luminous plane rather than reading as isolated pinpoints.
Slightly enlarge the particles to improve continuity and perceived softness of the plane without returning to the oversized foreground-bokeh look.
Reduce force positional influence to restrain the deep downward particle tail at t4 and preserve a thinner, more elegant horizontal sheet.
